newsitem.title: USA: Federal-Mogul to sell S. African units.
newsitem.headline: Federal-Mogul to sell S. African units.

text.p: Federal-Mogul Corp said Monday it agreed to sell its South African distribution operations to Chariot Holdings Ltd and its retail operations to Lexshell 16 Investment Holdings Ltd.

Terms of the two sales were not disclosed. Federal-Mogul said total annual sales in its South African aftermarket operations were about $120 million in 1996. The two units employ about 1,450 people in 57 retail stores, nine wholesale warehouses and a national distribution center.
In connection with the sale to Chariot, Federal-Mogul said the two companies will enter into supply and distribution arrangements for certain southern African markets, including South Africa.
The two sales are subject to various conditions and are expected to close in the second quarter.

The sales are part of Federal-Mogul's divestiture plan, annouced in February. The company said it remains committed to completing its restructuring in 1997 and focusing on growing its manufacturing operations.
"Our largest concentration of retail stores and distribution operations being held for sale were in South Africa," Federal-Mogul chairman and chief executive Dick Snell said in a statement.
Federal-Mogul said it had purchased the South African operations in 1994.
Last week, Federal-Mogul completed the sale of its Autralian aftermarket operations, also part of its restructuring plan.
Federal-Mogul provides parts for automobiles, light trucks, heavy trucks, and farm and construction vehicles.
